policy: A generated GLB remains a source candidate until it passes identity, volume, rear construction, material, pivot, scale, topology, LOD, and in-game performance review.

notes: The cardinal model preserves the thick octagonal lens housing and coherent rear mass.
The six-orbit model fuses the views into an elongated barrel and is rejected.
Remove loose internal filaments, correct orientation, and rebake the over-bright metal before runtime use.
The cardinal model preserves the open spindle cage and suspended crystal from every direction.
The six-orbit model contains an opaque rectangular background plane and is rejected.
Consolidate fine orbital strands and validate the crystal support before runtime use.
The cardinal model best preserves the green Tideglass chamber and asymmetric bronze cradle.
The six-orbit model changes the chamber to magenta and alters the cradle silhouette.
Increase minimum thickness and verify the pendant connection before runtime use.
The six-orbit model preserves the beacon head, glass vane, housing, and three-legged stance.
The cardinal model collapses into a textured plane and is rejected.
Correct the local forward axis, establish ground contact, and make gameplay LODs before runtime use.
The six-orbit model gives the strongest shelter volume and prop arrangement.
Both lanes bake a large ground slab into the mesh, so neither is runtime-ready.
Split the shelter, packs, lantern, and terrain into separate generation targets before reconstructing again.
The six-orbit model preserves the unequal Y-shaped fork and colored mineral tips.
The cardinal model loses one fork and is rejected.
Thicken the narrow vanes, set the ground pivot, and make gameplay LODs before runtime use.
